fields.title: Reestr: Launching a Feature Announced Yesterday by a Competitor
fields.summary: The biggest feature of the year launches in three weeks. Yesterday, a competitor announced a similar one. Decide how to launch.
fields.decisionPrompt: How will you structure the launch of this feature?
fields.brief/role: You lead product marketing at Reestr.
fields.brief/company: Reestr is an electronic document workflow service for small businesses. 1,800 paying companies, subscription model, 14-day free trial.
fields.brief/context: In three weeks, browser-based document signing with counterparties—the year's biggest feature—goes live. Yesterday, a competitor announced a similar feature "by the end of the quarter." A major accounting conference is next month, where a booth costs as much as two months of search ads.
fields.brief/objective: Ensure high feature adoption rather than mere awareness.
fields.brief/constraints: You, one copywriter, and half a designer. Three weeks until release. Budget covers either an event booth or a quarter of search advertising.
fields.brief/task: Decide how to structure the launch and explain your rationale.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Address the objection, not the competitor's announcement
fields.learnTakeaway/body: When a competitor announces the same feature, the temptation is to speak louder and earlier. But traffic driven by industry noise arrives with the same fundamental question; if your landing page fails to answer it, buzz changes nothing. The primary objection raised by your users and competitor comments is your core messaging topic. A single verified beta metric is worth more than any teaser.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content:
Visit → sign-up 8%, sign-up → first document 41%, first document → payment 37%.

Conversion varies by channel: search ads 3%, accounting Telegram channels 21%, referrals 34%.

Over the last two months, marketing scaled search ads: sign-ups grew from 450 to 900/month, while activated users rose from 184 to 207.

Analyst note: "Payments occur on day 14, but we calculate monthly conversion by dividing monthly payments by monthly sign-ups. With accelerating traffic, this artificially depresses conversion rate."
fields.evidenceCards/1/content:
The feature was beta-tested for three months across 19 companies.

A 12-person manufacturing firm reduced contract signing times from 4 days to 6 hours across its eight most frequent counterparties. Unchanged for others as they aren't onboarded. Client agreed to be named.

The remaining 18 use the feature, but baseline metric tracking was omitted.

The primary objection voiced across all beta users: "Will counterparties actually accept digital signing?" This is neither a feature issue nor a price issue.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content:
Post on their channel: "Counterparty signing coming by end of quarter." No demo, no beta, no pricing.

They have 6,000 paying clients and a channel audience triple your size. The post generated high engagement.

Half of the post comments ask: "Will counterparties accept this?"

Your Commercial Director messaged in slack: "We need to announce before them ASAP."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content:
Existing clients (1,800 companies) receive release notes: email open rate 31%, click rate 4%. Recent release notes read: "Optimized signature module, updated dependencies, added bulk select."

Accounting Telegram channels: ad placements are cheap; audience is cold but converts to sign-ups 3x better than search ads.

Upcoming conference: attended last year with the goal to "show the product," collected 60 business cards, converted zero sales.

The copywriter asks what to put on the landing page: currently it lists features.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Frame messaging around the main objection and launch iteratively
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Focus messaging on addressing "Will my counterparty accept this?", back it up with beta quantitative data, map text across customer touchpoints, rewrite release notes for existing clients, and skip the event booth budget.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence:
The landing page shifts focus from "Browser-based signing" to "Your counterparty will accept it—we send them a secure web link, no software required," backed by the manufacturing firm's 6-hour vs 4-day signing metric and explicit caveats.
Client release notes are updated: "Sign contracts with counterparties in hours; start with your most frequent partners." Click rates grow from 4% to 12%.
Ad spend shifts to accounting channels: sign-up conversion hits 21% vs 3% in search ads, generating higher total registrations at equal budget.
One month post-launch, 340 out of 1,800 accounts actively use the feature. The competitor hasn't launched theirs yet.
Trade-off: you skipped the conference and ignored the competitor's teaser publicly, annoying the Commercial Director for two weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Capitalize on market interest sparked by their post. Release an announcement this week highlighting your active beta.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence:
The announcement comes out in two days, gathers a noticeable response, and fifteen hundred clicks to the landing page.
The page remained a list of features: conversion to registration is 6%. Of those who registered, 19% reach their first document — well below the usual 41%, because they came to look at the announcement, not to solve a task.
The same question about the counterparty keeps appearing in the comments, and there is no answer to it anywhere.
Three weeks later, the feature itself comes out, but the occasion is already spent: the second announcement gets four times less.
Trade-off: you won a week of attention and spent it sending cold traffic to a page that doesn't answer the main question.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Set up a booth at the conference
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Target decision-makers directly at the venue next month. Invest budget into a booth to unveil the feature.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence:
The booth costs an entire quarter of search advertising. Two days yield 80 business cards and numerous discussions.
Lacking explicit success metrics, post-event ROI is unclear: follow-up emails sent to all 80 yield 6 replies and 2 scheduled meetings.
One conversation proves insightful: an accountant clarifies that fear stems not from digital signatures themselves, but from counterparties demanding paper originals later. This refines the core objection—at the cost of the quarterly marketing budget.
Trade-off: you overpaid for insights already visible in beta feedback while depleting funds for channels that convert 7x better than search ads.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Broadcast detailed release notes to existing base
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: You have 1,800 paying clients. Send comprehensive release notes to all accounts and add an in-app banner.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence:
The email goes out on launch day. Open rate matches baseline at 31%, while clicks show minor growth (5% vs 4%).
The issue lies in the messaging: copy reads like an engineering changelog, highlighting bulk actions and query optimizations before key features.
An in-app banner performs better: 260 companies open the feature, yielding 90 completed signatures.
New visitor acquisition remains completely unaddressed and the landing page stays untouched.
Trade-off: you engaged existing customers via low-cost in-app messaging, but failed to refine core positioning for external growth.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Conversion is viewed as a single aggregate metric without funnel stage or source breakdowns
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Acquisition growth is evaluated independently of downstream retention and usage
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Messaging focuses on product features without highlighting concrete user benefits or proof
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: The same message is recycled across all stages of user awareness and funnel steps
fields.rubric/remediation/4/gap: Market news is treated as actionable signal without evaluating if it alters strategy
fields.rubric/remediation/5/gap: Event participation lacks a verifiable objective or measurable success criteria
fields.rubric/remediation/6/gap: Release notes report internal engineering outputs rather than user value changes
fields.rubric/remediation/7/gap: Case study is presented without quantitative proof or context, offering no real evidence
